title: Ministry of Mines to Organise Roadshow on 8th Tranche of Critical and Strategic Mineral Block Auctions and NMEDT Workshop in Patna
body_text:
The Ministry of Mines, Government of India, is organising a Roadshow on the 8th Tranche of Auction of Critical and Strategic Mineral Blocks and a Workshop on the National Mineral Exploration and Development Trust (NMEDT) on 17 August 2026 in Patna, Bihar.
The programme will be chaired by Shri Satish Chandra Dubey, Union Minister of State for Coal and Mines, Government of India, in the august presence of Shri Samrat Choudhary, Chief Minister of Bihar, and Dr Pramod Kumar, Mines Minister, Government of Bihar. Senior officials of the Ministry of Mines, Government of Bihar, Geological Survey of India (GSI), Mineral Exploration and Consultancy Limited (MECL), industry representatives and prospective investors are expected to participate in the programme.
The 8th Tranche comprises 20 mineral blocks, including 3 Mining Lease and 17 Composite Licence blocks, covering a diverse range of critical and strategic minerals such as Graphite, Rare Earth Elements (REE), Rare Metals, Vanadium, Gallium, Titanium, Molybdenum, Tungsten, Potash, Phosphorite and Glauconite.
The Roadshow will provide prospective investors and industry stakeholders with an overview of the mineral potential of the blocks on offer, auction framework, bidding process and opportunities for investment and participation in the critical and strategic minerals sector. Detailed presentations will be made by MECL on the mineral blocks, SBICAPS on the mineral auction process and tender document, and MSTC on the e-auction process.
The programme will also include a presentation on the NMEDT Scheme for partial reimbursement of exploration expenses for Composite Licence holders, followed by an open-house discussion to facilitate interaction with stakeholders and address queries relating to the auction process.
The second half of the programme will feature a Workshop on Mineral Exploration: Planning, Execution and Reporting. The workshop will cover India’s mineral exploration potential, the National Geoscience Data Repository (NGDR), preparation of exploration blocks using NGDR, and preparation of mineral exploration reports, with technical sessions by senior officers of the Geological Survey of India.
The initiative reflects the Government’s continued efforts to promote exploration, accelerate the development of critical and strategic mineral resources, enhance private-sector participation and strengthen India’s mineral security. It also supports the broader vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat by facilitating greater domestic exploration and development of minerals essential for emerging technologies, clean energy and other strategic sectors.

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Mines is holding a Roadshow on the 8th Tranche of Critical and Strategic Mineral Block Auctions along with a Workshop on the National Mineral Exploration and Development Trust (NMEDT) on 17 August 2026 in Patna, Bihar. The 8th Tranche comprises 20 mineral blocks (3 Mining Lease and 17 Composite Licence blocks) covering minerals such as Graphite, Rare Earth Elements, Rare Metals, Vanadium, Gallium, Titanium, Molybdenum, Tungsten, Potash, Phosphorite and Glauconite. The event will feature presentations on the auction framework, e-auction process, NMEDT reimbursement scheme for exploration expenses, and a technical workshop on mineral exploration using the National Geoscience Data Repository (NGDR).
enrichment.context: India has been ramping up efforts to secure critical and strategic minerals essential for clean energy, electronics, and defence technologies, especially after amendments to the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act in 2023 that allowed the Central Government to auction blocks for minerals like lithium, REEs, and other critical minerals previously reserved for government agencies. Successive tranches of auctions (this being the 8th) reflect the government's push to reduce import dependence on countries like China for materials such as rare earths, graphite, and tungsten, which are vital for batteries, magnets, semiconductors, and defence applications. The NMEDT, funded through a cess on mining leaseholders, supports exploration activities and reimburses exploration costs, especially for private Composite Licence holders, addressing India's historically low private-sector participation in mineral exploration compared to global peers. The NGDR is a digital repository launched to democratize access to geoscience data, aiding private explorers in identifying and evaluating potential mineral blocks, which is part of a broader push for a National Mineral Exploration Policy. This roadshow, while primarily a promotional/investor outreach event, is part of a series of such state-level roadshows tied to the ongoing critical mineral block auction programme, and reinforces the government's efforts toward mineral security and Atmanirbhar Bharat in the mining sector.

prelims_questions.question: Consider the following minerals: 1. Graphite 2. Rare Earth Elements 3. Vanadium 4. Potash. Which of the above are included in India's list of Critical and Strategic Minerals being auctioned under the block auction scheme?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release lists Graphite, Rare Earth Elements, Vanadium, and Potash among the minerals covered in the 8th Tranche of Critical and Strategic Mineral Block auctions.

prelims_questions.question: The National Mineral Exploration and Development Trust (NMEDT) is primarily aimed at:
options: Reimbursing exploration expenses of mineral licence holders
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, the NMEDT provides partial reimbursement of exploration expenses for Composite Licence holders, supporting private-sector mineral exploration.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of critical and strategic minerals for India's economic and strategic security. Evaluate the effectiveness of the mineral block auction mechanism introduced after the 2023 MMDR Amendment Act in achieving self-reliance in this sector.

Examine the role of institutional mechanisms like the National Mineral Exploration and Development Trust (NMEDT) and the National Geoscience Data Repository (NGDR) in promoting private-sector participation in mineral exploration in India.

related_articles.relationship: Both concern the same overarching mineral-sector regulatory framework under the MMDR Act; the recently passed amendment reshapes taxation and stability rules for the very mineral blocks being auctioned in this roadshow.

related_articles.title: MMDR Amendment Bill, 2026
related_articles.relationship: This backgrounder explains the MMDR Amendment Bill 2026, which establishes the Centre-directed fiscal and regulatory framework governing mineral rights and leases, directly relevant to the mineral block auction process being promoted in the new release.
